THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.

The petitioner/claimant has filed this Miscellaneous First Appeal being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded vide judgment dated 01.08.2019 passed in M.V.C.
No.1090/2018 by the learned VI Additional District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Belagavi (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal").
2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
On 28.01.2018, the petitioner was proceeding by walk towards Hunashikatti village to meet his relatives.

sentences.text: While he was crossing the road, the rider of a Hero Honda CD 100 motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-24/E-9690 was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries including multiple fractures.
The petitioner underwent treatment and spent a huge amount.
Thereafter, the petitioner filed a claim NC: 2026:KHC-D:3635 HC-KAR petition under Section 166 of the MV Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
3. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company filed its statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.
It contended that the petitioner was crossing the road without looking into the side of the road, and that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner while crossing the road.
It was further contended that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
The Insurance Company, however, admitted that the offending motorcycle was insured with the Insurance Company.
Hence, on these grounds prays to dismiss the claim petition against the Insurance Company.

Shri. Vinayaka S/O. Gopal Pattar vs Kalmesh S/O. Mayappa Hattaraki on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38194859/
2 4.
The owner of the offending motorcycle filed a statement of objections contending that the vehicle was insured with Insurance Company.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Based on the rival pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed the relevant issues.
6. To substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1, examined the Doctor as PW-2 and marked 15 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3635 HC-KAR documents as Exs.P-1 to P-15.

Conversely, on behalf of the respondents, the Insurance Company examined three witnesses as RW-1 to RW-3, and marked eight documents as Exs.R1 to R8.
7.

The Tribunal, after appreciating the verbal and documentary evidence on record, allowed the claim petition in part with costs vide Judgment dated 01.08.2019 and the petitioner entitled for compensation of 1,44,600/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the realisation of the amount, and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the said compensation amount.
8.
The petitioner, being dissatisfied with quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, has filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

9. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and also learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company.
10.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the accident is of 2018.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the notional income as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (KSLSA).

As per the said schedule, the notional income for the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3635 HC-KAR relevant year is at 11,750/- per month, whereas the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at 3,000/- per month, which is on the lower side.
He also submits that to prove the disability, the petitioner examined the doctor as PW-2, who has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 35%.
However, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 10%, which is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the petitioner has not produced any income proof.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income at 3,000/- per month.

He further submits that the accident was caused due to the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner, and the Tribunal was justified in fastening the liability to the extent of 25% on the petitioner.
He submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and do not call for any interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

12. Perused the records, and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: The point, that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.
14. It is an undisputed fact that the petitioner met with an accident, sustained grievous injuries and a charge sheet is filed against the rider of the motorcycle.
The petitioner has produced the charge sheet, marked as Ex.P-7.
From the perusal of the charge sheet, it discloses that it is filed against the rider of the motorcycle.

It is also observed that normally, the pedestrian walk on the right side of the road, and the petitioner-during the cross examination has admitted that while he was trying to cross the road he met with an accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly recorded a finding that the petitioner contributed to the negligence in the accident, and assessed the liability to the extent of 25% and whereas the contributory negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle was assessed to the extent of 75%, which is just and proper.
I do not find any grounds insofar as fastening the liability to the extent of 25% on the petitioner, and 75% on the Insurance Company.

Regarding quantum of compensation:
15.
Admittedly, the petitioner was aged about 19 years as on the date of accident.
The accident is of 2018.
The NC: 2026:KHC-D:3635 HC-KAR petitioner contended that he was working as a goldsmith and was earning more than 20,000/- per month.
To substantiate the case of the petitioner, the petitioner has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of income proof, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the notional income of the petitioner as per the schedule issued by KSLSA.
On the contrary, the Tribunal has assessed the monthly income at 3,000/-, which is on the lower side.

As the accident is of the year 2018, this Court reassesses the notional income at 11,750/-
per month.

Applying the multiplier of '18' for the petitioner's age group, as per the proposition of law laid down in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) AND OTHERS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.
16.

sentences.text: The petitioner also examined the Doctor as PW-2 to prove the disability.

The Doctor has deposed that he had examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically, and issued a disability certificate marked as Ex.P10 and opined that the petitioner has suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 35%, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 10%, which is on a lower side.

Considering the evidence of PW-2 and the medical records, this Court is of the opinion that the NC:
2026:KHC-D:3635 HC-KAR compensation awarded by the Tribunal requires to be reassessed and accordingly the disability in assessed at 15%..

Accordingly, this Court reassesses the compensation under the following heads:

2 Pain and suffering 25,000/- 40,000/-
 3 Food and nourishment  2,000/- 5,000/-

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of 5,27,200/- as against 1,44,600/-
awarded by the Tribunal, i.e., to an enhanced compensation of 3,82,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its deposit.
In view of the same, the point regarding the quantum of compensation is answered accordingly.

ORDER
(i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 01.08.2019, passed in M.V.C.No.1090/2018 by the VI Additional District Judge and Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Belagavi is hereby modified.
